findings.claim: --since filtered whole transcript FILES by mtime then summed every record in them, over-reporting a long session touched minutes ago in full.
findings.note: Hard-verified against REAL transcripts, since this feeds the loop-cost deliverable. (a) The filter does real work: over the last 30 min the same 6 files yield 154 requests per-record vs 172 file-granular. (b) rec_time matches the actual format — every record uses ISO-8601 with a literal Z ('2026-08-30T19:12:43.593Z'); the .replace('Z','+00:00') makes it parse on pre-3.11 Pythons too, and .timestamp() yields UTC epoch, the same basis as `date +%s`. (c) `undated` cannot inflate the number: 0 of 17,353 billed records in the whole project corpus lack a timestamp, and a live run reports undated:0. (d) The bool guard is right (True would otherwise read as epoch 1s and be silently dropped) and the 1e11 millis heuristic separates cleanly (now ~1.7e9 s vs ~1.7e12 ms). (e) mtime pre-filter reasoning is sound and safe in the only direction that matters: it can only exclude files whose LAST append precedes the cutoff, which by append-only construction cannot hold a later record; a touched/copied file is over-kept, never under-kept. (f) sidechain is set before the `continue`, so a partially-in-window subagent still reports sidechain:true (verified on live rows). (g) Images are counted only inside kept records, so a screenshot in an out-of-window record no longer inflates a windowed total. (h) The tests are not tautologies: the old file-granular code gives requests 3 / input 700 against the fixture, the tests demand 2 / 600, and JSON.parse(stdout) implicitly pins the undated note to stderr. Shape unchanged apart from the additive `undated` key.
